name: Reflow
explanation: This criterion requires that content can reflow into a single column at narrow viewport widths without forcing the user to scroll in two directions to read it. Specifically, at a viewport 320 CSS pixels wide (roughly what you get zooming a 1280px-wide design to 400%) or a viewport 256 CSS pixels tall for content that scrolls sideways, the page must still work with only vertical scrolling — no horizontal scrollbar needed to read a line of text. In practice this means a responsive layout: columns stack, sidebars move below or collapse, and fixed-width elements give way to fluid ones. There are specific exceptions for content that genuinely needs two-dimensional layout to make sense — data tables, maps, diagrams, images, video, and games — those are allowed to require scrolling in both directions. This is different from SC 1.4.4 Resize Text, which is about 200% browser zoom preserving readability generally; 1.4.10 is specifically about the reflow behavior at 320px/400% and banning two-dimensional scrolling for ordinary content.
whoItAffects: People with low vision who use high browser zoom levels (often 300-400%) or a fixed large text size rather than a screen magnifier, since magnifiers already pan in two dimensions but zoomed browser content should not force that extra effort. It affects people with physical or motor disabilities who find horizontal scrolling significantly harder than vertical scrolling, particularly anyone using a switch device, head pointer, or limited fine motor control where tracking a scroll position in two axes at once is error-prone. It also affects anyone reading on a small device — a phone in portrait orientation, a screen split side-by-side with another app — where a layout that assumes desktop width becomes unusable rather than merely cramped.
howToTest: Open the page in a desktop browser and use the browser's responsive design / device toolbar mode (or manually shrink the window) to set the viewport to exactly 320 CSS pixels wide. Alternatively, at a standard 1280px-wide layout, zoom the browser to 400%. Then scroll down through the entire page using only vertical scrolling and check whether you ever need to scroll sideways to read a sentence, reach a button, or see a form field. A horizontal scrollbar appearing for genuinely two-dimensional content (a wide data table, a map, a diagram, an embedded video) is acceptable; a horizontal scrollbar needed to read ordinary paragraph text, navigation, or a form is a failure. Also check that no content is cut off or overlapping as the layout reflows.

check.question: A page requires horizontal scrolling to read body text when the viewport is set to 320 CSS pixels wide. Which of these is true about SC 1.4.10 Reflow?
choices: This is always acceptable because some horizontal scrolling is expected on narrow screens
This is a failure, because ordinary content must reflow to avoid two-dimensional scrolling at 320px width
This is only a concern if the user is also using a screen reader
This is acceptable as long as the content is technically readable by scrolling in both directions
